0.long_answer: The radioactive isotope most commonly used after surgery for papillary or follicular thyroid cancer is iodine-131, often referred to as I-131 or radioiodine. I-131 is selectively absorbed by thyroid tissue, which makes it an effective treatment for eliminating any remaining thyroid cells after surgical removal of the thyroid gland. This targeted approach minimizes damage to surrounding healthy tissues while reducing the risk of cancer recurrence.
